parts.label: a.i
parts.display_text: A spectral line has wavelength 434 nm for a stationary source and is observed at 502 nm from a receding astronomical source. State whether this is a redshift or a blueshift, and what the shift indicates about radial motion.

answer.text: It is a redshift: the observed wavelength is longer. In the Doppler interpretation, the source is receding from the observer.

sup-1aa072d7093cc8f1-q15:whole.hint: Compare the observed wavelength with the laboratory wavelength before calculating the speed.
notes: For radial speeds much smaller than c, Δλ/λ₀ ≈ v_r/c. Use the rest wavelength λ₀ in the denominator.
Longer observed wavelength indicates recession and shorter wavelength approach. Keep the low-speed approximation separate from the relativistic Doppler relation when speeds are large.

ibd-56ec7b86c6b34d97-q16:whole.hint: First decide whether the source and observer are getting closer or farther apart.
notes: For sound, source motion changes the spacing of wavefronts; observer motion changes how quickly they are encountered. Choose the Doppler signs so approach increases observed frequency.
For collinear motion, f_obs = f_source(v ± v_observer)/(v ∓ v_source), with speeds measured relative to the medium. Do not simply exchange source and observer speeds.

cross-ca24m1-26:whole.hint: Decide whether the source is moving towards or away from the observer along their line of sight.
notes: Approach compresses the arriving wavefronts and raises the observed frequency; recession spreads them and lowers it. The source frequency stays unchanged.
For a source passing to one side of an observer, consider the component of motion along the source–observer line. This question needs qualitative reasoning, not the higher-level Doppler formula.
